To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) callus induction was enhanced in MS medium supplemented 2,4-D (2,5 mgL-1) and Kin(1,0 mgL-1).
air desiccated callus of BRRI dhan 32 and BRRI 47 showed better performance for plant regeneration and salt tolerance.
the air desiccation treatment was found to be an effective technique for the enhancement of in vitro callus regeneration in salt tolerant rice genotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective and reliable in vitro protocol for regeneration of rice plants from calli under salt stress.
the optimization of in vitro regeneration of 3 rice genotypic calli in the presence of abiotic stress factors.
the development of a simple and cost effective method for the production of plantlets of rice genotypes under abiotic stress conditions through in vitro regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of air desiccated pretreatment and NaCl induced salt stress can be used for enhancing the regeneration efficiency of callus cultures of rice.
air desiccated callus pretreatment could be an efficient technique to improve the regeneration capability of rice callus under abiotic stress conditions.

BRRI dhan 32 was the best genotype for in vitro regeneration, BRRI dham 47 showed the best tolerance to abiotic stress, and air desiccated BRRI dhan-47 showed the best performance to abiotic stress and regeneration efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

air desiccated callus could survive in NaCl salt stress and gave higher number of plant regeneration compared to controls; and the highest regeneration (88.80%), tolerance index (0.20%), RWC (10%) and relative growth rate (1.03%) was observed in BRRI dhan 47 with 45 h of air desiccated 4 weeks old BRRI dhan-32 calli.
, the present study could be used to develop a protocol for the regeneration of salt and drought tolerant rice genotypes through in vitro technique.
the air desiccation is a better pretreatment for calli to enhance their regeneration efficiency in rice and it also enhances their tolerance to salt stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the in vitro plant regeneration of rice could be enhanced by partial air desiccating calli before sub-culturing.
air desiccated callus showed better regeneration capability than control calli and the best genotype was BRRI dhan 32 for callus initiation and BRRI dha47 for regeneration under abiotic stress.
air desiccated callus can be used as a source of explant for regeneration of plants under abiotic stresses.
